detail.longDescription:
Okay, this just got interesting!

I installed the opencode-web-deepsearch plugin and gave Qwen3.8 access to web search (DuckDuckGo).

So naturally, I had to test it xD

First I asked it to search for recent news about NetBSD. That sounded useful, but of course there was always the possibility that some of it was hallucinated.

So I tried something where I could actually verify the results: I asked it in German how the 2026 state election in Saxony-Anhalt turned out.

Qwen searched the web, tried to get the results from Tagesschau, noticed that the actual numbers were hidden in charts and SVGs and then performed a second, more specific search for the percentages and seat distribution.

It came back with the correct result: AfD 43.8%, CDU 17.2%, SPD 9.3%, Greens 8.9%, Left 8.6%, BSW 5.3%, with the AfD getting 39 of 83 seats.

I checked the result against current sources afterwards and the core numbers were correct.

It even spent several minutes researching instead of just making up an answer. The whole thing took 9 minutes and 18 seconds xD

There was one factual mix-up in the final answer, though: it confused the constitutional protection classification in Saxony with Saxony-Anhalt.

So Qwen3.8 definitely isn't infallible. But this is honestly way more impressive than I expected from a local 27B model.

All instructions were in German, the research was done in German and the model actually used the web to find and cross-check information.

Local AI is getting ridiculous! Now we just need affordable GPUs with enough VRAM...

RX 6700 XT, 12 GB VRAM, 16 GB RAM, 32 GB swap
